title: EVAP Purge Valve Replacement
summary: EVAP blueprint for confirming purge valve sealing, command response, and leak-test evidence before replacement.
symptoms: EVAP code with little or no drivability symptom
Rough idle after the purge valve sticks open
inspect_first: Purge valve command response and sealing when commanded closed
Smoke-test evidence for leaks before replacing valves
EVAP hoses, canister, vent valve, fuel cap, and filler neck condition
Connector fit, wiring, and vacuum routing around the purge valve
likely_causes: Purge valve stuck open or leaking when closed
Purge valve solenoid not responding to command
EVAP hose leak or canister issue blamed on the purge valve
Vent valve or fuel cap problem creating similar EVAP codes
repair_overview: Confirm purge valve sealing or command failure before replacement.
Inspect routing, connector, and hose condition around the valve.
Replace the purge valve and reconnect hoses without creating new leaks.
Clear codes and verify EVAP command response or monitor readiness when possible.
common_mistakes: Replacing the purge valve without smoke testing leak codes
Ignoring vent valve, fuel cap, filler neck, or canister faults
Missing a stuck-open purge valve after hard-start-after-fueling complaints
Breaking brittle EVAP hoses during quick replacement
estimate_guidance: Quote smoke testing or EVAP diagnosis when leak location is not proven.
Add hose or connector repair only when inspection supports it.
Note hard-start-after-refueling or fuel odor context when it supports purge valve failure.
Verify purge command and sealing before presenting the repair as confirmed.

recommended_repairs.title: EVAP Smoke Test
recommended_repairs.description: Use before replacing valves when the code points to a leak rather than proven purge failure.

recommended_repairs.title: EVAP Vent Valve Check
recommended_repairs.description: Vent-side faults can overlap with purge and leak codes.

recommended_repairs.title: Fuel Odor Inspection
recommended_repairs.description: Use when fuel smell, refueling complaints, or tank-area leak clues are part of the story.

diagnostic_context.intro: EVAP purge valve estimates should follow command, sealing, and smoke-test evidence so leak codes do not turn into parts guessing.
